annotations.text:
CHH-F05 — Location-Aware Events (CHH-37; US-CHH-005-01/02/03/04/07/08)
Mobile row above, web row below. Every screen ships both, per design/ui-standard.md Breakpoints.
Built from the CHH-F05 Confluence spec including §6 (attendance marking, organiser controls, analytics).

ATTENDANCE IS MARKED BY THE ORGANISER, FULL STOP. QR check-in (US-CHH-005-06) is out of scope for this story and has been removed from the design; there is no scan flow, no QR panel at the desk and no scan-method column anywhere. Two boards cover attendance: Mark attendance (005-07) and the attendance dashboard (005-08).

Decisions carried from the approved draft:
1. RSVP IS GREEN. ui-standard.md lists RSVP under --clay but "Confirm attendance" under --go. The AC's literal label is "RSVP" and it is the commitment, so it takes b-accept on --go. Needs a one-line ruling in the standard.
2. The organiser has NO notification-radius control. US-CHH-005-05 AC1 notifies everyone whose registered location is in the venue's region — it is a read-only reach statement, not a slider.
3. Event types are the spec's four: Blood Donation Camp · Health Camp · Awareness Session · Other.
4. Full events show a disabled button reading "Event Full" (005-03 AC2); RSVP'd events read "You're going" (AC3). There is no waiting list.
5. Attendee contact is masked in organiser lists (§6.4 asks for a contact-safe user reference). Blood group is not a spec'd event field and is not shown.
6. The attendee's RSVP reference (A24) stays — it is how the organiser finds the right person to mark, not a scannable code.

HOW STATES ARE DRAWN (same convention as CHH-F03 and CHH-F04)
Each artboard carries one AC-state tweak chip rather than a separate file per state.

CreateEvent — top | details (the two halves of the form)
CreateEventWeb — invalid | valid. Only the failing state was on the approved review page; the valid values are the mobile filled frame's, unchanged.
Discovery — list | loading | empty (AC2 empty-state sentence is the spec's, word for word)
DiscoveryWeb — list | gpsDenied
EventRsvp — before | going
EventEditWeb — edit | cancelConfirm
ManualAttendance — results | searchTooShort

Static artboards (one state on the approved page): EventRsvpWeb (Event Full), EventManageMobile (started, cancel blocked), ManualAttendanceWeb (AC3 unauthorised), EventAnalytics, EventAnalyticsWeb.

STILL OPEN — the spec does not decide these, so they are flagged, not invented.

• RSVP to several events at once — §4 Question 1 is Open. Every frame assumes yes; a no needs a blocked-RSVP state.
• Walk-ins (§6.1, "if allowed by product policy") — not drawn. Manual attendance leaves room for an "Add a walk-in" action.
• Organiser overrides of the attendance window and the capacity cap are "explicitly enabled and audited" — drawn as blocked states with no override affordance until someone says who holds that permission.
• Attendance correction (§6.3 — reason at least 10 characters, audit logged) appears only as an audit line; no correction flow yet.
• Cancellation reason is drawn as required and shown verbatim. AC2 requires the notification, not the reason field.

NOT DRAWN YET: post-event feedback (§6.2/§6.4 — the dashboard has a Feedback tab with no artboard behind it), the attendance-correction flow, walk-in registration, per-channel delivery status behind "340 notified", and guest access (whether an unregistered guest may RSVP is a role-matrix question for the PRD; every frame assumes a registered individual).

OUT OF SCOPE for CHH-37: QR-code check-in (US-CHH-005-06) — removed 2026-09-05. If it ever comes back it is a separate story and a separate artboard.

CHH-F05 OFF-APP DELIVERY — push, SMS and toasts for events.

Every channel carries the same facts in the same order: what, when, where, how far (approximate), spots remaining. Never a patient name, a requester identity or an exact address.

Push actions are RSVP (--go, b-accept — the commitment) and Not now (neutral secondary). Success toasts stay on --leaf: a toast confirms, it does not commit.

SMS is the only channel for a donor with no app. No buttons — reply YES to RSVP, NO to stop. One segment each. A cancellation is a statement, not an offer, so it carries no keyword.
